definitions.explanation: The first child born to a couple. A somewhat literary or traditional term.

examples.japanese: {初子|ういご}の{名前|なまえ}を{決|き}めるのに{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took time to decide the name for our firstborn.

examples.japanese: {初子|ういご}は{両親|りょうしん}にとって{特別|とくべつ}な{存在|そんざい}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that the firstborn child is a special existence for parents.

notes:
Composed of {初|うい} (first, initial) + {子|ご} (child). A classical reading — the more common modern equivalent is {第一子|だいいっし} or {最初|さいしょ}の{子|こ}. Also sometimes written as {初|うい}{児|ご}.

USAGE:
- Somewhat literary and traditional; found in formal writing, historical texts, and family-related contexts
- In everyday conversation, {第一子|だいいっし} or {一人目|ひとりめ}の{子|こ} is more common
- Can also be read as はつご, though ういご is the primary reading

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {初子|ういご}が{生|う}まれる: a first child is born
- {待望|たいぼう}の{初子|ういご}: a long-awaited firstborn
- {初子|ういご}を{授|さず}かる: to be blessed with a first child

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {長男|ちょうなん}: eldest son — specifically male
- {長女|ちょうじょ}: eldest daughter — specifically female
- {第一子|だいいっし}: first child — the modern formal equivalent
- {末っ子|すえっこ}: youngest child — the opposite position in birth order
